concerns.text: The plan assumes a 4-bit quantized 8B model (Llama-3-8B-Int4) can run on a CPU-only GitHub Actions runner (2 vCPU, 7GB RAM) within 10 mins/task. Inference of 8B models on CPU typically requires 15-30+ minutes per task and often exceeds 7GB RAM due to Python overhead and context loading, making the 6-hour total runtime for ~100 tasks infeasible on the specified free-tier hardware. The 'GPU escape hatch' to Kaggle is not a guaranteed free resource for CI and introduces non-reproducibility.

The research plan acknowledges the CPU runtime will exceed 6 hours (16 hours estimated) and proposes reducing the sample to 30 tasks. This reduction severely compromises statistical power for a Chi-squared/Fisher's test on error distributions, likely rendering the study unable to detect the hypothesized effect (task-dependence of error types). The plan relies on a sample size that is statistically underpowered for the stated research question.
